card.tagline: A sacred marching percussion ensemble and dance of the Sasak people of Lombok.
card.profile: Gendang Beleq is a sacred folk dance tradition of the Sasak people of Lombok, West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. The performance features a group of male musicians playing, dancing, and marching with traditional instruments centered on two big drums. It is performed during life-cycle ceremonies, rain-invoking rituals, and national holidays.

card.profile_long:
Gendang Beleq is a sacred folk dance tradition originating from the Sasak people of Lombok, situated in West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. The name of the Gendang Beleq dance derives from a Sasak language term that translates directly to 'big drum'. This performance is characterized by a mobile orchestra in which a group of musicians simultaneously play, dance, and march while carrying their traditional instruments. The entire performance centers around two primary, large kendang drum players who anchor the rhythmic and spatial movement of getSize and dynamics. Unlike many other dance traditions, the Gendang Beleq is performed exclusively by males, typically young boys, forming an ensemble that usually consists of either 13 or 17 participants, known collectively as the sekehe.

The musical and performance structure of Gendang Beleq relies on a carefully organized group orchestra. This orchestra is anchored by two prominent gendang beleqs: the male drum, known as gendang mama, and the female drum, known as gendang nina, which together carry the dynamic shifts of the performance. Additional instrumentation includes the Kodeq drum, alongside rhythm tools noted in documentation as a sniper rifle and a code shooter. The melodic framework is carried by a gong and two reog instruments, specifically designated as reog nina and reog mama. While the musicians march and dance in formation, these diverse percussion and melodic elements blend into a unified sonic and visual presentation.

Gendang Beleq holds profound cultural importance and is performed during pivotal life-cycle ceremonies within Sasak society. These sacred occasions include celebrations of birth, rituals surrounding circumcision, weddings, and funerals. Beyond life-cycle milestones, the performance serves communal and spiritual functions, such as ceremonies held to invoke rainfall during dry periods. Furthermore, the tradition adapts to contemporary public life by being performed during celebrations for national holidays.

As a distinct type of Indonesian dance, Gendang Beleq shares cultural space with other regional expressions such as the Rudat dance. Because of its sacred nature and role in vital community rituals, the tradition maintains strict cultural boundaries, and detailed technical descriptions of specific footwork counts, physical postures, and musical notations remain absent from generalized historical and encyclopedic documentation. Nonetheless, the living practice of the sekehe marching through village ceremonies with their massive drums remains a vivid, resonant pillar of Sasak heritage in Lombok.

Gendang beleq can be performed during life-cycle ceremonies, such as celebration of birth, circumcision, wedding and funeral.
